disposition_mapping.rationale: The council converged, against the maximalist position, that KB-03's cutoff discipline requires a discrete, auditable lock event with an affirmative human confirmation, not a dissolution into ambient continuous monitoring. Checklist distribution and status-pulling are automated (a standards-silent matter), but the close manager retains a real, logged confirm-and-lock action and override authority, plus a named degraded-mode fallback owner for weaker-infrastructure contexts, addressing emerging_economy's and agentic_architect's concessions.

Near-unanimous council agreement that this step conflates mechanical (template-driven) and estimation-based (judgment-driven) postings that carry different standards obligations. The mechanical stream is automated with logged, reversible postings and exception review (KB-01 preserved); the estimation stream retains a named accountable preparer with documented basis (KB-04, KB-05, KB-10, KB-12), kept structurally separate from management review to satisfy R2R-R-05.

Against maximalist's proposal to fold allocations into an undifferentiated background job routed through a generic exception queue, the majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer) is followed: allocation-basis validity is a distinct, silent-failure-mode judgment that decays without a named domain-expert owner. The monthly run is automated; a periodic basis-governance review with a named owner is retained as a distinct function.

Unanimous agreement to split high-volume rule-based matching (automatable, but kept fully auditable including near-misses to protect IFRS 10 completeness per accounting_standards' and agentic_architect's concerns) from mismatch resolution, settlement and elimination preparation, which remains a distinct, explicitly resourced human function per R2R-R-02, KB-14, and emerging_economy's resourcing non-negotiable.

Matching is automated and produces aged exception lists, but certification remains a genuine human attestation act for every account — light-touch for low-risk, full evidence review for high-risk — rather than accepting an automated match rate as certification. This resolves the council's unresolved conflict on 'what counts as certification' in favour of accounting_standards' and hitl_designer's position, satisfying R2R-R-01 and KB-02.

FX translation, elimination posting and TB roll-up are automated as deterministic computation (KB-07), but against maximalist's 'validate only flagged variances' framing, the majority (pragmatist, finance_domain, emerging_economy, hitl_designer, agentic_architect) is followed: the financial accountant validates full entity submissions, and exchange differences remain a distinct visible line (KB-08), because flag-only review cannot detect errors that don't cross a tolerance threshold.

Strong majority position (hitl_designer, finance_domain, accounting_standards, pragmatist, emerging_economy, and maximalist's own concession) that management review must not be reduced to approving a pre-filtered anomaly list. The controller retains full visibility into the complete comparative population, with automation used only to accelerate surfacing, preserving R2R-R-07, R2R-R-04 and KB-02's fair-presentation requirement.

Compilation of statements and schedules is automated from signed-off inputs, but against maximalist's 'radically reduced labour' framing, emerging_economy's fair-presentation objection is followed: commentary authorship requiring market and operating intuition remains human, alongside a release gate that structurally enforces R2R-R-03 and R2R-R-04 as system preconditions, satisfying R2R-R-06.

steps.description: An orchestration platform continuously pulls subledger status (AP, AR, fixed assets, payroll) against the close calendar and distributes checklist tasks automatically, but cutoff enforcement remains a discrete, auditable event: the close manager performs an affirmative, logged readiness-confirmation and posting-lock action, not an ambient or purely continuous state. This preserves IAS 1 period-discipline (KB-03) as a decision point, resolving the council's event-versus-continuous conflict in favour of a named human gate. The platform raises two distinct, separately-logged escalation types to the close manager: business exceptions (a subledger reports not-ready) and infrastructure exceptions (feed timeout, malformed data, tool unavailability), so the manager can tell 'the business isn't ready' apart from 'the integration broke.' The close manager holds real, exercised override authority (proceed with documented gap, delay, force-lock), every action logged. Entities without reliable system integration run a documented manual fallback procedure with a named owner for subledger confirmation and lock; this fallback is a first-class path, not an edge case.
steps.name: Close orchestration and cutoff gate

steps.description: Recurring accruals and prepayment releases governed by fixed templates and amortisation schedules are system-generated and posted by a rule engine, preserving the accrual mechanism (KB-01): recognition on occurrence, not cash movement. Every automated posting is logged with the rule/template that fired and is reversible prior to the next close gate. Postings outside a defined variance-from-prior-period tolerance are queued, not auto-posted, for GL accountant review; the GL accountant certifies each period's run rather than re-keying every line. A named manual-preparation fallback owner exists for entities or periods where source data is late, semi-digitised or manually re-keyed. Reduced mechanical-posting volume is paired with a named transition path: displaced preparer capacity moves toward exception review and toward supporting the estimation function in TS-03, not an unstated headcount reduction.
steps.name: Automated mechanical journal processing
outputs: System-posted mechanical journals with rule/log trail

steps.description: Provisions, bad-debt/expected-credit-loss estimates, inventory NRV write-downs, litigation accruals, reclassifications and error corrections remain human-prepared with a documented judgment basis (IAS 8 KB-04, KB-10; IFRS 9 KB-12) and preserve the error-correction path required by KB-05. Modelling tools may generate a suggested figure (e.g., an ECL model output or aging-based suggestion) but only propose; a named preparer of record posts and attests to the basis, with a second reviewer for material estimates. This actor is structurally distinct from the controller performing management review (TS-09), satisfying R2R-R-05.
steps.name: Estimation and judgment-based journal entries
outputs: Estimation journals posted with documented basis and evidence

steps.description: Cost and overhead allocations (shared-service recharges, corporate overhead distribution, intercompany management fees) run automatically each period against the validated allocation model, with anomalous or out-of-tolerance allocations queued for review. A named allocation-basis owner, distinct from the cutoff-exception handler and possessing allocation-model expertise, performs a periodic (not necessarily every-cycle) governance review of whether drivers, cost-centre weightings and ownership percentages still reflect the business, because allocation drift is silent and does not throw a system error. Basis changes are logged with who authorised them and when, preserving traceability where the accounting-standards knowledge base is otherwise silent on allocation methodology.
steps.name: Allocation processing with named basis ownership

steps.description: High-volume, rule-based matching of intercompany balances (AR/AP mirror accounts, loans, recharges) runs continuously with full transaction-level logging. Both matched items and near-misses within tolerance are recorded on a visible, auditable log, not only hard mismatches, so that a matching-tolerance setting cannot become an unauditable de facto definition of 'eliminated in full' under IFRS 10 (KB-14). A periodic human completeness attestation confirms the matched population is what it purports to be, addressing the risk that an exception-only design cannot itself demonstrate completeness.
steps.name: Automated intercompany matching

steps.description: Mismatches requiring inter-entity coordination, counterparty negotiation, transfer-pricing checks and management arbitration are resolved by a named, explicitly resourced intercompany accountant role — not assumed absorbed by tooling, given that shared-service centres often concentrate this expertise in one or two people. This role processes settlements/netting and prepares elimination entries, satisfying IFRS 10's completeness requirement (KB-14): unresolved items remain tracked to resolution rather than dropped silently from the elimination population.
steps.name: Intercompany exception resolution, settlement and elimination preparation

steps.description: Reconciliation matching (GL to subledger, GL to bank, GL to supporting schedules) is automated and produces an aged, flagged list of unreconciled items, with every auto-match logged with the rule that fired and reversible. Certification requirements continue to follow the existing risk rating: low-risk, high-volume accounts receive a light-touch human certification — a genuine attestation act, not a pass-through of an automated match rate, per KB-02's evidential-trail requirement. High-risk, judgmental and historically-aged accounts retain full manual preparation, evidence review, and reviewer sign-off at the seniority the policy requires. Unreconciled items are aged and escalated automatically.
steps.name: Risk-tiered GL and balance-sheet reconciliation
outputs: Reconciliation certifications (light-touch and full) with evidence

steps.description: Trial balance roll-up, FX translation (IAS 21, KB-07) and elimination/minority-interest posting are automated, deterministic, logged and reversible computations. Exchange differences remain a distinct, visible reported line (KB-08), never netted invisibly inside a variance-flagging layer. The financial accountant validates the full consolidated output against entity submissions — not only system-flagged variances — because elimination incompleteness or an FX anomaly that does not cross a tolerance threshold would otherwise be invisible to a flag-only reviewer; this is the last human checkpoint before results reach management review. Any change in consolidation computation or policy is surfaced for disclosure rather than silently embedded (KB-06).
steps.name: Consolidation, FX translation and elimination validation
outputs: Consolidated balances validated against full entity submissions

steps.description: The controller reviews the full population of consolidated results and comparatives — not a pre-triaged or pre-cleared subset — with an automated variance/anomaly-detection tool acting strictly as an augmentation layer that surfaces and ranks deviations for faster review while leaving the full underlying comparison accessible for drill-down. The controller investigates anomalies (flagged and unflagged), determines and documents management adjustments, and signs off account-level results. This actor is structurally distinct from the TS-02/TS-03 preparers, and any decision-support agent used here shares no posting authority with the journal-preparation functions.
steps.name: Management review and adjustments

steps.description: Financial statements, variance schedules and KPI summaries are compiled/drafted automatically from signed-off consolidated results and validated data, then staged for review. The group reporting accountant retains authorship of management commentary and narrative — informed by market and operating context that automated drafting lacks — and holds the final release/distribution gate. The package cannot be staged or distributed until reconciliation (TS-07) and management review (TS-09) are both complete, enforced as a system precondition rather than a calendar convention.
steps.name: Financial reporting package compilation and release
outputs: Reporting package distributed with authored commentary
